data.text:
Nagpahayag ng pasasalamat si Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos kay business tycoon Ramon Ang matapos ang pangako nitong tutulong siyang resolbahin ang problema sa baha sa Metro Manila.

“Thank you! What else can I say?... ‘Yung proposal ni Ramon Ang is certainly very welcome because we’ve seen his projects. Maganda naman ang mga nagiging resulta, he’s able to bring it on time. You know the man is an engineer, so I’m sure pinag-aralan niya nang mabuti ‘yan,” saad niya sa press conference tungkol sa flood control nitong Lunes, August 11, 2025.

Nitong Biyernes, nagboluntaryo si Ang ng libreng tulong para matuldukan na ang paulit-ulit na baha. Sinabi rin ni Marcos na ang kondisyon lamang ni Ang ay dapat asikasuhin ng mga lokal na pamahalaan ang problema sa basura.

“I will certainly look at this proposal of Ramon very, very closely and see if we can do it. Like I said it will require coordination between LGUs and I guess San Miguel… Any offers of help are always welcome,” ani Marcos.

data.text:
Before DDS rush to boycott McDonald’s in their area, they might want to pause and think about who they’re really affecting.

Nationwide, McDonald’s Philippines—through Golden Arches Development Corporation (GADC)—runs a mix of company-owned and franchised stores. As of July 2025, about 51% are GADC-owned, while 49% are operated by local sub-franchisees. While there’s no city-specific ownership breakdown for Davao, applying the national trend suggests that roughly half of the 22 McDonald’s branches in the city could be locally owned franchises, with the rest run directly by GADC.

That’s the thing about boycotting a big global brand—you might think you’re targeting a corporation, but you could just as easily be hurting a neighbor. That McDonald’s on the corner might be owned by a local family who’s been quietly supporting the poor and disadvantaged in your own community.

data.text:
‘HIHILAHIN TAYO SA AYAW AT SA GUSTO NATIN’

According to President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos, the Philippines can’t stay out of conflict if a war breaks out in Taiwan, given our close geographical proximity and the number of OFWs in the said country.

“We do not want to go to war but I think if there is a war over Taiwan, we will be drawn. Hihilahin tayo sa ayaw at sa gusto natin, kicking and screaming we will be drawn and dragged to that mess,” he explained in a press conference on Monday.

He also addressed the comments of China, stating he’s “playing with fire” regarding his stance on the issue.

“I don’t know what they are talking about. Playing with fire? I was just stating facts,” he said.
